## feature

## fix

### Row groups batch across write_rows calls

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The reproduction measured 2000 single-row calls producing 2000 row groups and 3.68 MB against 1 group and 3.6 KB batched; three new tests lock row-group count, batch-boundary flushing, and abort logging.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

1. `StagedWriter.write_rows` flushed every call, so the round-2 streaming pipeline wrote one tiny Parquet row group per pair and per finding — a 1024x size inflation on the reproduction.
2. The buffer now spans calls, flushes at `WRITE_BATCH_ROWS`, and flushes the remainder on `close_publish`; `abort()` discards it (the staged file is unlinked).
3. The abort test also closes the round-2 follow-up: cleanup failures are logged with `exc_info` and never raise.

#### before

Findings and comparison Parquet files grew ~1.8 KB per row in row-group metadata alone under per-row streaming writes.

#### after

Row groups are bounded by the configured batch size (65,536 rows); the 2000-row reproduction writes one group.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`tests/test_parquet_io.py::test_write_rows_batches_across_calls`, `test_write_rows_flushes_at_batch_size`, `test_abort_logs_cleanup_failures_and_never_raises`; reproduction at `/tmp/repro_round3.py` (3.68 MB vs 3.6 KB measured).

:::

### INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE decisions state their blocking reason

```
level: high
```

#### reason

Reproduced first (status MISSING_EVIDENCE, zero findings), then fixed and locked by a test asserting the finding content and the decision reason codes.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `TechnicalAssessment.feed` now emits a WARNING finding for every INSUFFICIENT_OBSERVATIONS or MISSING_EVIDENCE row: the comparison reason code, affected datasets, observed counts, and the policy minimum (for insufficient observations).
2. The codes propagate into the decision row's `reason_codes` automatically, so an INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE decision explains itself.

#### before

A decision could be INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with only `IDENTITY_DECLARED_NOT_VERIFIED` in its reason codes.

#### after

The same decision carries `TECH_BELOW_MIN_OBSERVATIONS` (or the missing-evidence reason) with counts and the minimum in the findings table.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`tests/test_policy.py::test_insufficient_observations_produce_findings_and_reason_codes`.

:::

### Findings stream out as they are produced

```
level: high
```

#### reason

A 12-dataset uncalibrated run streams all 793 findings (66 pairs x 12 rows + identity) exactly once with sequential unique IDs — the emission path is complete and duplicate-free.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The pipeline emitted component findings before the pair loop, each technical finding as `feed` returned it, the finalize tail, then the fastp finding; retained per group are only the component findings (bounded by dataset count) and a unique reason-code list.
2. `finalize_group_decision` takes `tech_reason_codes` instead of a findings list and returns only the findings it creates; `evaluate_group` derives codes for its callers.
3. A first cut returned component findings twice from `finalize_group_decision`; the finding-ID determinism test caught the aliasing before commit.

#### before

One group's technical findings (O(pairs x metrics) under an uncalibrated policy) accumulated in memory before a single end-of-group emission.

#### after

In-memory finding state per group is the bounded component list plus a small code list; the StagedWriter batches rows.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`tests/test_e2e.py::test_uncalibrated_findings_stream_completely`, `test_finding_ids_deterministic`.

:::

### Native thread pools limited at runtime

```
level: high
```

#### reason

Direct measurement: OpenBLAS runs 12 threads before and after the late env changes and 1 thread when the env is set before import; two new tests introspect actual pool settings after `_worker_init`.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `_worker_init` set `OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL_NUM_THREADS` with `setdefault` after NumPy loads — provably ineffective; the README's per-worker cap claim was false in effect.
2. `threadpoolctl` (new explicit dependency, pixi + pyproject) limits the pools at runtime: per worker in `_worker_init`, and to `ResourceConfig.main_threads` around the main-process comparison stage; the controller stays referenced so garbage collection cannot undo it.
3. `pyproject` gained a mypy override (threadpoolctl ships no types).

#### before

BLAS pools ran at full core count regardless of the `--threads` budget; the README claimed otherwise.

#### after

Pool settings are verified by test (<= 1 and <= 2 threads after init, surviving `gc.collect()`); the README states the runtime mechanism and why env defaults are insufficient.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`tests/test_resources.py`; subprocess measurement in `/tmp/repro_round3.py` (12 vs 1 threads).

:::

## limitation

### The comparison stage is clamped to the documented remainder budget

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Stated because a reviewer may expect the comparison stage to use all cores once workers finish; the behavior follows the README's documented budget rule.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `ResourceConfig` assigns `main_threads` (the remainder) to the main process, and the comparison loop is clamped to it even when scan workers are already done.
2. The measured effect is within noise (worker-4 CLI run: 3.02 s vs 2.94 s); relaxing it would contradict the documented rule.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`benchmarks/results-2026-10-22.json` worker_scaling entries; `src/seqconsistency/models.py` ResourceConfig docstring.

:::

## observation

### Clean re-measurement after discarding a contended run

```
level: high
```

#### reason

Both runs are in the record; the contrast quantifies what contention does to these benchmarks.

#### description

```
type: [table]
```

| Workload | Round-2 baseline | Contended (discarded) | Clean re-run |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pair scaling 5 ds | 0.627 s | 1.215 s | 0.669 s |
| Pair scaling 40 ds | 61.97 s | 68.43 s | 64.89 s |
| SE FASTQ | 127.7k reads/s | 124.0k | 129.5k |
| BAM | 64.1k rec/s | 57.7k | 59.2k |
| Peak RSS 600k reads | 959.7 MiB | 958.9 MiB | 958.8 MiB |

The contended run showed a uniform 1–10% slowdown on code paths round 3 never touched (FASTQ, BAM scans) with the largest distortion on the shortest measurements — the contention signature. The clean run (started at load1 1.72 under the tightened gate) puts pair scaling within noise of baseline (+3.6–6.8%); memory is flat everywhere.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [table]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`/tmp/bench-r3.log` (gate at load1 3.99) vs `/tmp/bench-r3b.log` (gate at load1 1.72); `benchmarks/results-2026-10-22.json`.

:::

## process

### discarded a contended benchmark instead of committing it

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The first post-fix run started at load1 3.99 — inside the old gate but visibly loaded; the uniform cross-path slowdown contradicted the code diff, so the numbers were discarded rather than rationalized.
2. The gate was tightened (load1 < 2, load5 < 3) and the re-run committed.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`/tmp/bench-r3.log` vs `/tmp/bench-r3b.log`; comparison table in the observation above.

:::

### a first-cut refactor duplicated component findings

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The first version of the finalize refactor returned `all_findings` (component + tail), so both the wrapper and the pipeline would have emitted component findings twice.
2. The finding-ID determinism test caught the aliasing (two list slots, one object, one final ID) before commit; the return contract is now "only findings this function created".

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Session log (test run before commit `ea3c06d`); `tests/test_policy.py::test_finding_ids_deterministic`.

:::
